# epftoolbox2

> Python library for electricity price forecasting research. It downloads market data (ENTSO-E, Open-Meteo, calendars, CSV), builds leak-free features, runs rolling-window forecasts with one model per period of day, horizon and run day, and evaluates them. `DataPipeline` produces one DataFrame, `ModelPipeline` fits models and returns an `EvaluationReport`, and `Workflow` runs both from YAML. Install with `pip install epftoolbox2` (Python 3.11 or newer).

This file is an index. Read the rules below, then open only the pages you need. Links are repo-relative paths to the page sources. The same pages are published at `https://dawidlinek.github.io/epftoolbox2/<slug>/`, where `<slug>` is the path under `docs/src/content/docs/` without its extension, for example `data-pipeline/overview/`.

Rules to know before using the library:

- **Time zones.** Every source returns a UTC index. Set the market zone once with `DataPipeline(timezone="Europe/Warsaw")`. `TimezoneTransformer`, `CalendarSource` and `OpenMeteoSource` inherit it when their own zone is unset, and the dates and keywords (`"today"`, `"today_d+7"`) passed to `run()` then mean local calendar days.
- **DST.** A local day has 23, 24 or 25 hours. Nothing invents the missing 02:00 hour. Day lags shift by local calendar days, not by 24 hours. Training rows are chosen by date, and a slot the clock doesn't have on the issue or target day is not planned. `DSTNormalizeTransformer` gives every day 24 slots when a model needs them.
- **Column names** are relative to the row's local date D. `x_d-k` is `x` on D-k and `x_d+h` is `x` on D+h as known on D. Targets are `{target}_d+{h}`. Predictors may contain `{horizon}`, for example `"temperature_2m_d+{horizon}"`, or be callables `(horizon)` or `(horizon, hour)`, or a whole-list function of `ctx` that picks each forecast's list before any fit.
- **Transformer order:** `TimezoneTransformer`, `ResampleTransformer`, `ImputeTransformer`, feature transformers (`DailyProfileTransformer`, `DailyStatsTransformer`, `PeriodStatsTransformer`, `RollingStatsTransformer`, `SolarGeometryTransformer`, `LambdaTransformer`, `DSTNormalizeTransformer`, which `SolarGeometryTransformer` must precede), then `LagTransformer`. Lagging a UTC index shifts by UTC days and is wrong around every DST switch.
- **Information set.** A forecast issued on day D may only use values known at issue time. `ModelPipeline(issue_time="11:45", issue_timezone="Europe/Brussels")` compares every predictor and the newest training target with it before any fit. `availability` says what follows: `"warn"` (the default with an issue time) lists late inputs and columns without a rule in `report.availability()`, a warning, the terminal exporter and the manifest, and goes on; `"raise"` refuses them with `InformationSetError` (use it for published results and CI); `"none"` (the default without an issue time) checks nothing. The level doesn't change forecasts, and changing it alone resumes a run. `InformationSet()` defaults to 11:45 Europe/Brussels, 15 minutes before the 12:00 CET gate closure. The check reads names; `pipeline.verify(df, test_start, test_end)` or `epf verify` tests the boundary empirically at every level, and only status `ok` passes (`leak` and `inconclusive` don't). `pipeline.explain(df, model=..., test=(start, end), horizon=1, hour=12)` shows what each predictor holds relative to the target day T = D + horizon. A rule's `vintage` class says what the archive holds (`latest_revision`, `snapshot`, ...): it moves no number, `report.vintages()` lists it and comparisons of models reading one series with different classes warn. A list of rules with disjoint `.during(valid_from=, valid_until=)` periods is a lag that changed; a value no rule holds for is never known. Another pipeline's stored forecasts come back as a column through `ForecastSource`, known from that pipeline's issue time on its data zone's dates (`published(..., day_zone=)`); outside a `Workflow` pass `information_set.with_source_rules(data_pipeline.sources)`, or the column has no rule.
- **Leak-free inputs.** Realised values such as `load_actual` and `generation_*` are known only as `_d-1` or older, and a rolling window of them (`RollingStatsTransformer`) only with `lag_days=1`. `load_forecast` is usable unshifted or as `_d+1`, and `_d+2` and later are look-ahead. The source pages list the safe shifts for every column.
- **Open-Meteo.** `{variable}_d+i` is the forecast for the same local hour on D+i, taken from runs initialised at or before D at `run`:00 UTC (`run` defaults to `"00"` and is a UTC hour, not a local issue time). `api="previous_runs"` (default) has the long archive and caps `horizon` at 6 (`jma_seamless`, `gfs_seamless`, `ecmwf_ifs025`, `ecmwf_ifs`) or 5 (`icon_seamless` and other models), so `d+7` needs `api="single_runs"` (horizon 1 to 14, shorter archive). `horizon=None` picks the largest value without look-ahead. A zone is required, directly or from the pipeline.
- **Data cache.** `pipeline.run(start, end, cache=True)` keeps one cache per source under `.cache/sources/`, keyed by its `get_cache_config()`. The last two days before now are never recorded as cached, so a daily run sees newly published data. A cached range is not revised, so clear the cache to pick up provider revisions. `cache="file.parquet"` stores the whole source output in one file instead.
- **Resumable training.** `ModelPipeline.run(..., save_dir="results")` writes one JSONL file (or, with `save_format="parquet"`, one Parquet directory) and one manifest per model and computes only the missing tasks on a rerun. Results made with a different configuration raise `ManifestMismatchError`.
- **Validation and test.** `run(df, validation=(start, end) | "previous_year", test=(start, end))` forecasts both windows in one run, and each forecast is bit for bit what a plain run over its window gives. `report` is the test window, and `report.validation` holds only forecasts whose target day is before the first test issue day; choose on that, never on the test window. `validation` alone leaves the test period untouched.
- **Ensembles.** `pipeline.add_ensemble(AverageEnsemble(members=[...], top=None | k | "validation", name=...))` averages stored forecasts on the keys all averaged members hold, and counts the rest as `member_missing` in `forecast_counts()`. `top` chooses on validation per test period, on the keys every member holds with a finite prediction and actual and a target day before the first test issue day, and has test forecasts only; `report.choices()` says what it chose. `ModelPipeline.report()` computes ensembles from stored results. Members with another issue time, or another value in a column they share, raise; `choices()` has `validation_share` and warns on a thin choice; a `top=1` ensemble is an exact clone of its member, which counts once in a Holm family and is one model to `mcs()` and `ranks()` (`df.attrs["clones"]`).
- **Training boundary.** For a run day D the training targets end at D-1, unless a model has `newest_target="published"`: then they are every target its rule says is known by the issue time (needs an information set), and never a row dated D or later. A model with `refit="7D"` or `"1MS"` (OLS, LassoCV, Ridge, LEAR, and the networks, whose default is `"7D"`) fits once per calendar block instead of per forecast, and a forecast issued on D trains on what one issued on the block's first day (its refit day, on or before D) trains on, so its targets end before that day. Horizons are 1 to `horizon` days ahead (7 by default), or only those `horizons=[1, 3, 7]` lists, each forecast the same as in the full run. Forecasts are issued on every day of the test period, or only on the weekdays `issue_days=["friday"]` lists (training is unchanged). Each (period of day, horizon, run day) is one task in a process pool, so on Windows (which spawns workers) scripts that call `run()` at top level need an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard.
- **Daily frames.** `freq="1D"` fits one model per day on a frame with one row per local date, all at one time of day, cut with `df.at_time("12:00")` after the transformers. The row's time of day is read from its index and is what `x_h-1` counts back from, so stamp it at the time of the forecast, not at midnight. `EconomicEvaluator` can't score such a run.
- **Missing values.** A NaN predictor skips that forecast. Skips are counted, never dropped silently. `report.forecast_counts()` shows planned, produced and missing forecasts per model, and `summary()` and every `by_*()` table have a `forecasts` count per model and group; a `by_*()` table warns when the models of a group differ in it. Compare models only on identical forecast keys and report how many forecasts each produced.
- **Breakdowns and daily series.** `by_quarter()`, `by_day()` and `by_price_level()` run every evaluator on each group alone, so models are compared on the forecasts they share inside it. The price level comes from the actual only, with one spike threshold (`df.attrs`) for all models. `report.aggregate("1D", agg="max")` scores daily maxima, minima, means or spreads (or `"peak"`/`"offpeak"` block means, `peak_hours=(8, 20)`) from hourly or 15-minute forecasts, counting only whole days (23/24/25 hours, 92/96/100 quarter-hours) or whole blocks; `aggregate("1h", agg="mean")` turns 15-minute results into hourly ones, an hour counting only with all four quarter-hours; dropped days and hours are in its `forecast_counts()`. `by_column(column, bins=None)` groups forecasts by a source-data column at the target row (joined as `CsvExporter(extra_columns=)` joins), and `error_split()` divides a 15-minute model's squared error into day level, hour profile and quarter shape. `report.join(other)` merges the models of separate runs (same frequency, distinct names).
- **Significance.** `report.tests(benchmark=...)` compares each model with a benchmark on the keys the pair shares and prints `n_days`, `n_forecasts` and the number of models `m` behind its Holm correction. `report.mcs()` and `report.ranks()` run on the keys all models share. A per-hour DM test (`by="hour"`) is descriptive, never a verdict, and one test year resolves differences of about 5 % of the MAE.
- **YAML.** `DataPipeline`, `ModelPipeline` and `Workflow` have `save(path)` and `load(path)`. `save()` writes the ENTSO-E key as `${ENTSOE_API_KEY}` and `load()` expands it from the environment. Pass `include_secrets=True` only for files you never commit. Callable predictors cannot be saved (`save()` raises `TypeError`), so use `{horizon}` templates; a module-level function of `ctx` is saved by its import path. An unregistered class name raises on load.
- **Custom components** must be registered in `COMPONENT_REGISTRY` to load from YAML, see the Extending page.
- **Extras and weights.** A family that needs an extra or pretrained weights has a model card; `run()` and `verify()` check every model's extra, runtime packages and weights before any fit, and never downloads: fetch weights first with `epf weights fetch <Model>` (`--accept <licence>` for a non-commercial or revenue-capped one). `report.provenance()` gives each such model's licence, weights and contamination verdict per window.
- **Examples.** Runnable scripts are in `examples/` and need `ENTSOE_API_KEY` in the environment, except `lear_lago.py` (LEAR on the Lago benchmark, downloaded from Zenodo) and `mlp_search.py` (a random search of `MLPDailyModel`s averaged by `AverageEnsemble(top=4)`, on the same benchmark; `[torch]` extra). Each has a `main()` that takes its date ranges and, if it writes files, an output directory. Worked snippets are on the two Examples pages.

- [Installation](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/installation.mdx): requirements, free-threaded Python setup, process environment variables and platform notes
- [Quick Start](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/quickstart.mdx): a first data pipeline and a first forecast
- [CLI Reference](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/cli.mdx): the `epf` commands, flags and interactive wizards

## Data pipeline

- [Data Pipeline Overview](docs/src/content/docs/data-pipeline/overview.mdx): sources, transformers, validators, date formats and local-day semantics of `DataPipeline.run()`
- [Pipeline Examples](docs/src/content/docs/data-pipeline/examples.md): from a minimal ENTSO-E pipeline to a full Polish one with weather and validators
- [Data Caching](docs/src/content/docs/data-pipeline/caching.mdx): per-source cache, single-file cache, what is recorded as cached, cache keys and clearing
- [Serialization](docs/src/content/docs/data-pipeline/serialization.md): YAML format of a `DataPipeline`, secrets, relative paths and the timezone key

## Data sources

- [EntsoeSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/entsoe.mdx): ENTSO-E load, price, generation, transfer and installed capacity, with output columns and safe shifts
- [OpenMeteoSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/openmeteo.mdx): archived weather forecasts by cutoff run, models, horizon limits and several locations
- [EnergyChartsSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/energy-charts.mdx): keyless Energy-Charts forecasts by vintage, actuals, day-ahead prices and flows, with licence, rate limits and availability rules
- [CalendarSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/calendar.mdx): holidays, school holidays, weekday, hour, month and daylight features
- [CsvSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/csv.md): time series from a CSV file
- [EpftoolboxBenchmarkSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/epftoolbox-benchmark.mdx): the five benchmark datasets (NP, PJM, FR, BE, DE) of Lago et al. (2021)
- [PseSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/pse.mdx): the Polish TSO's reports API without a key: load, SDAC price in PLN, wind and PV, flows, with availability rules
- [ForecastSource](docs/src/content/docs/data-sources/forecast.mdx): another pipeline's stored forecasts as a column at their target instants, or a day statistic of them (`agg`), known from its issue time on its data zone's dates, what it refuses and how it caches

## Transformers

- [TimezoneTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/timezone.mdx): UTC index to local time and daily values onto local midnight
- [ResampleTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/resample.mdx): one regular frequency without inventing data
- [ImputeTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/impute.mdx): gap filling with leak-safe methods only
- [DSTNormalizeTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/dst-normalize.mdx): exactly 24 (or 96) slots per local day
- [DailyProfileTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/daily-profile.mdx): a local day's hourly values copied onto every row of that day
- [DailyStatsTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/daily-stats.mdx): per local day minimum, maximum, mean, last value and peak mean
- [PeriodStatsTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/period-stats.mdx): per local hour mean of 15-minute data and each row's deviation from it, known when the hour's last slot is
- [LambdaTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/lambda-transformer.mdx): custom column arithmetic or a full custom transform without a new class
- [SolarGeometryTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/solar-geometry.mdx): the sun's elevation, its sine, a clear-sky irradiance and a night flag at the middle of each period, over one site or a weighted mean, static (known at any time)
- [RollingStatsTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/rolling-stats.mdx): a statistic of a column's complete days over a window of local days ending `lag_days` before the row's, such as the capacity proxy `generation_solar_roll365max_d-1`, judged at the window's newest day
- [LagTransformer](docs/src/content/docs/transformers/lag.mdx): `_d-k` and `_d+k` lag columns by local calendar day

## Validators

- [Validators overview](docs/src/content/docs/validators/overview.md): which validator catches what and how to read the results
- [DSTStructureValidator](docs/src/content/docs/validators/dst-structure.md): rows per local day (23, 24 or 25 hours)
- [CoverageValidator](docs/src/content/docs/validators/coverage.md): index checks and per-column coverage and missing runs
- [PlausibilityValidator](docs/src/content/docs/validators/plausibility.md): value ranges such as SDAC price limits and frozen constant runs
- [EdaValidator](docs/src/content/docs/validators/eda.md): exploratory statistics shown in the terminal

## Model pipeline

- [Model Pipeline Overview](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/overview.mdx): `ModelPipeline.run()`, predictors, pre-fit data checks and parallelism
- [Model Pipeline Examples](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/examples.md): complete `ModelPipeline` usage examples
- [Working with Results](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/results.md): `EvaluationReport` breakdowns (including quarter, day and price level), daily aggregates, joining reports, forecast counts and raw predictions
- [Comparing Models](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/comparing-models.md): `tests()`, `mcs()`, `ranks()`, `compare()`, `leaderboard()` and how to read them
- [Incremental Training](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/caching.mdx): `save_dir` results, resuming and the manifest
- [Serialization](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/serialization.mdx): YAML format of a `ModelPipeline`
- [Forecast-Only Mode](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/forecasting.mdx): operational forecasts for the next days without back-testing, and a short note on the engine
- [Information Set](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/information-set.mdx): availability rules, vintage classes and rules over time, the issue-time check at the levels none, warn and raise, `report.availability()`, `report.vintages()`, `pipeline.explain()` and the leakage probe
- [Verifying a Pipeline](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/verification.mdx): `ModelPipeline.verify()` and `epf verify`, the leakage probe on sampled issue days with a positive control
- [Time and Calendars](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/time-and-calendars.mdx): which rows a forecast trains on, by date, which forecasts are planned, what a clock change does, `aggregate()` on switch days, and old results refused on resume
- [Training Windows](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/training-windows.mdx): `training_window` as days, `"expanding"` from the frame's first date, or a list of windows averaged inside one model, all or nothing per forecast, `member_predictions`
- [Predictor Functions](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/predictor-functions.mdx): a function of `ctx` that picks each forecast's list, what `published()` and `value()` mean at each availability level, how each list trains, `Use(list, train_on="matching")`, resuming and YAML
- [Validation and Test](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/validation-and-test.mdx): `run(df, validation=..., test=...)` and `"previous_year"`, records identical to plain runs, `report.validation`, resuming validation before test, SLURM merges
- [Ensembles](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/ensembles.mdx): `AverageEnsemble` and `add_ensemble()`, the rule of the average, what counts for choosing, why a `top` ensemble has no validation forecasts, `report.choices()`, SLURM merges and YAML
- [Hyper-parameter Search](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/hyperparameter-search.mdx): choosing settings on validation only: the default random loop averaged by `AverageEnsemble(top=4)`, `run(validation_every=k)` scoring every k-th validation day, and `tune.BayesSearch` (`[tune]`, Optuna) with successive halving, identical keys per rung, the frame cut before the first trial, `SearchResult.best()` models with their provenance in `report.choices()`, warm starts and `epf tune --workers N` on a shared journal
- [Predictor Presets](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/presets.mdx): LEAR and expert-model inputs in this library's column naming
- [Several Zones](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/zones.mdx): `run(data={zone: frame})` runs every model per zone into `save_dir/<zone>/`, each zone's records those of its frame alone, `issue_timezone="data"` for each zone's own clock, `PanelReport` with `log_gain()` and `cells_lost()` over cells on their common keys, resuming and `verify` over zones
- [Generation Targets](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/generation.mdx): a solar or wind forecast from solar geometry, a capacity proxy or the installed capacity, fitted on the capacity factor with `normalise_by`, `bounds` and `zero_when`, and what the checks and `verify` say
- [Chaining Pipelines](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/chaining.mdx): one pipeline's out-of-sample forecasts as another's input through `ForecastSource`, known from the upstream's issue time, the coverage of the training rows, late upstream inputs, `chained_inputs` compared on resume; a 15-minute `ShapeModel` on a chained hourly forecast
- [The Engine](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/engine.mdx): `ModelPipeline(engine="on")` runs OLS, Ridge, LassoCV and LEAR (`"lars"`) of many variants in engine groups (one read of the data and one pool per refit rule), fitted from shared exact sums (`scaler="standard"` or a VST; LassoCV and LEAR `"cv"` from KFold blocks of the rows): the same bits alone, in any group, over array tasks and at any process count; within 1e-8 (OLS, LassoCV, LEAR) / 1e-9 (Ridge) of `engine="off"` with the same penalty and kink, every fit the sums can't give to those digits (each reason and bound listed: distance in the fit's own metric, OLS 30, LEAR and LassoCV 10; OLS refined by one step and a forecast whose estimated remaining error, from the raw sums' rounding, is above 5e-9; Ridge its rounding budget; a VST's inverse at most 3x the median of its training slopes) fitted as `"off"` does, to the bit; LEAR `"cd"` identical to `engine="off"`; `fit_path: "engine-2"` compared on resume (`"engine-1"` refused for every class, though only OLS's numbers moved); `engine="check"`; `ENGINE_MAX_MODELS` / `ENGINE_MAX_COLUMNS`; memory and the measured speed, 10,000 OLS variants on 12 cores included
- [Week-ahead Forecasting](docs/src/content/docs/model-pipeline/week-ahead.mdx): daily minimum and maximum load for D+3 to D+9 issued on Fridays, or for D+1 to D+7 every day with lists that drop what isn't published, against a TSO's forecast as a `NaiveModel`, and the settings that reproduce a published study

## Workflow

- [Workflow](docs/src/content/docs/workflow/overview.mdx): YAML experiment orchestration, environment settings, overrides and SLURM array jobs of one model or a block per task

## Models

- [Common Parameters](docs/src/content/docs/models/common-parameters.mdx): the parameters every model shares, and generation targets: `normalise_by` (targets divided by a column such as a capacity, the forecast multiplied by the issue row's), `bounds` (clipped after scaling back) and `zero_when` (0 with no fit where a column is 1), columns checked as inputs, not regressors
- [OLSModel](docs/src/content/docs/models/ols.mdx): ordinary least squares
- [LassoCVModel](docs/src/content/docs/models/lasso.mdx): Lasso with cross-validated regularization
- [RidgeModel](docs/src/content/docs/models/ridge.mdx): ridge regression whose penalty is chosen on every fit by leave-one-out from a grid
- [LEARModel](docs/src/content/docs/models/lear.mdx): LEAR (Lago et al. 2021), a Lasso whose penalty is chosen by AIC or BIC on the LARS path, refitted exactly or by Lago's coordinate descent, or by blocked 5-fold cross-validation (`criterion="cv"`, old `LassoLarsCV`, no refit); `LEARModel.lago()` reproduces the original epftoolbox's forecasts; the recommended settings are an `AverageEnsemble` of four `LEARModel`s, one per VST
- [Benchmark Reproduction](docs/src/content/docs/models/lear-benchmark.mdx): LEAR and Ridge on the five Lago et al. (2021) datasets, against the original epftoolbox and the published forecasts, and the recommended settings against `lago()`, on identical keys
- [NaiveModel](docs/src/content/docs/models/naive.mdx): one column's value on the issue row, such as a published forecast taken as a benchmark; with an information set, no forecast where the value wasn't out at the issue time
- [Residual Model](docs/src/content/docs/models/residual.mdx): `ResidualModel(base, learner)`, a base's out-of-sample forecasts (its own run over a warm-up, `<name>.base.jsonl`) plus a learner fitted on their residuals, the learner's list naming `base_fc_d+{horizon}` and `base_fc_hHH_d+{horizon}`; `HistGBModel`, scikit-learn's histogram gradient boosting pooled over the periods of a day, one thread a fit; `presets.tree_predictors`
- [Shape Model](docs/src/content/docs/models/shape.md): `ShapeModel(base, learner)` in a 15-minute run, a chained hourly forecast (`base`, read on the issue row; a warning where it isn't chained) plus a learner of each quarter-hour's deviation from its hour's actual mean, trained on natively 15-minute target dates only (`native="distinct"` or a date); the learner brings its window, refit, scaler and newest target
- [Gradient-Boosted Trees](docs/src/content/docs/models/trees.mdx): `LightGBMModel`, `XGBoostModel`, `CatBoostModel`, pooled over the periods of a day (`periods="pooled"`, the default) or per period, L1 and an expanding window weekly by default; one extra per package (`[lightgbm]`, `[xgboost]`, `[catboost]`; `[gbm]` the first two), imported by the first fit; `threads` per fit, the package's version (and XGBoost's `device`) compared on resume; also `ResidualModel` learners
- [PooledModel](docs/src/content/docs/models/pooled.md): one fit over the zones of a run of several markets, each zone's rows scaled within its own fit, `over=("zone", "horizon")`, a one-hot zone, every zone's training rows judged at the earliest issue of the day
- [Scalers and VSTs](docs/src/content/docs/models/scalers.mdx): standard scaling and variance-stabilising transformations (asinh, mirror-log, polynomial, N-PIT) for spiky prices
- [Neural Networks](docs/src/content/docs/models/neural-networks.mdx): `TorchModel` (a `torch.nn.Module` of your own, `output="day"` on day-level predictors or `"period"`, flat predictors or named blocks, saved by import path and source hash), the `MLPHourlyModel` and `MLPDailyModel` presets, the `[torch]` extra, `epftoolbox2.nets`, and the trainer's rules: seeds from the fit alone and their mean in EUR/MWh, early stopping on each fit's own training days, padded stacks bitwise the same as alone, one torch thread and TF32 off per fit, recorded and compared; torch stacks: the vmap-stacked models of a loop that share a stack key train together on one device, bitwise each model's own run (any module on a GPU, only `nets.MLP` with l1/mse on a CPU; `TORCH_STACKS=off` runs each alone, `=check` compares a sample)
- [Licences and Weights](docs/src/content/docs/models/licences-and-weights.mdx): model cards of families that need an extra or pretrained weights, the pre-flight before any fit, `epf weights fetch` (never during a run; `--accept` for restricted licences), runtime and weight hashes compared on resume, contamination verdicts and `report.provenance()`

## Evaluators

- [MAEEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/mae.md): mean absolute error
- [RMSEEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/rmse.md): root mean squared error
- [rMAEEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/rmae.md): relative mean absolute error
- [BiasEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/bias.md): mean error
- [ShapeMAEEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/shape-mae.md): error of the shape within each hour, for 15-minute forecasts
- [NMAEEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/nmae.md): MAE divided by the mean actual on the same forecasts
- [ScaledMAEEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/scaled-mae.md): mean of each error divided by a source-data column, such as capacity
- [DMEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/dm.md): MAE ratio, bootstrap interval and Diebold-Mariano test against a benchmark
- [MCSEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/mcs.md): model confidence set
- [EconomicEvaluator](docs/src/content/docs/evaluators/economic.md): profit of a battery scheduled on the forecasts

## Exporters

- [TerminalExporter](docs/src/content/docs/exporters/terminal.md): results as tables in the terminal
- [ExcelExporter](docs/src/content/docs/exporters/excel.md): formatted Excel workbook
- [CsvExporter](docs/src/content/docs/exporters/csv.md): wide-format CSV

## Reference

- [API Reference](docs/src/content/docs/reference/api.md): constructor and method signatures of the pipelines, `Workflow`, `EvaluationReport` and every shipped component
- [Extending the Library](docs/src/content/docs/reference/extending.md): custom sources, transformers, validators, models, evaluators and exporters
- [Release Notes](docs/src/content/docs/reference/release-notes.md): breaking changes and what they need from you, newest first

## Optional

- [examples/](examples/): runnable scripts for a data pipeline, a model pipeline, a full workflow, a YAML workflow, forecast-only mode and 15-minute forecasting

- [data_pipeline.yaml](data_pipeline.yaml): a saved `DataPipeline` with ENTSO-E, Open-Meteo and calendar sources
- [model_pipeline.yaml](model_pipeline.yaml): a saved `ModelPipeline` with models and evaluators
